note: Verifies type-safety, reactivity granularity, state aggregation, and async-race semantics of Angular 22 Signal Forms against Reactive Forms. No timing. Every value below is deterministic for the pinned versions and is reproduced by run.sh into probe-result.json.

experiment_A_type_safety.claim: A field-name typo and a wrong-type write survive to runtime under stringly-typed Reactive Forms access, but are compile errors under Signal Forms.
experiment_A_type_safety.caveat: IMPORTANT honesty note (the post states this too): Angular 14+ typed forms DO catch a wrong-type write when the control is reached by a statically-known literal path, e.g. group.get('user.email').setValue(42) is a compile error. The 0-error result is specifically the stringly-typed surface the post scopes its claim to: an unknown key group.get('emial') (always AbstractControl | null, so a typo never type-checks) and a dynamic/runtime path group.get(fieldName) (AbstractControl<any> | null). Both are idiomatic for dynamic and deeply-nested forms. Signal Forms have no stringly-typed escape hatch, so both bugs are always caught.

experiment_B_reactivity_granularity.claim: A consumer that reads only `email` does not re-run when the unrelated `age` field changes; Reactive Forms' group.valueChanges runs the consumer for any child change.
experiment_B_reactivity_granularity.method: Zoneless Angular effect() reading f.email().value() vs group.valueChanges.pipe(map).

experiment_C_state_aggregation.claim: Marking the deepest leaf touched buckets up to the intermediate group and the root; the root's touched computed recalculates exactly once; validity aggregates from descendants and recovers without a manual revalidate.
experiment_C_state_aggregation.method: form({user:{name,email},age}) with required(user.name); read touched()/valid() at leaf, group, root.

experiment_D_async_race.claim: Changing the value mid-flight aborts the in-flight async validation via AbortSignal; the stale result is dropped and only the latest completes.
experiment_D_async_race.method: validateAsync backed by resource(); a manual gate holds both loaders in flight; trigger 'taken' then 'free'.
experiment_D_async_race.caveat: This verifies the abort SEMANTICS, not that Signal Forms is uniquely safe. As the post states: Reactive Forms' AsyncValidatorFn also unsubscribes a superseded validation; the difference is mechanism (RxJS unsubscribe vs resource invalidation + AbortSignal). And in both, whether real network/CPU work actually stops depends on the loader honoring AbortSignal — cooperative cancellation.

cited_not_measured.claim: Async validation only runs after all sync validators pass (no network call while `required` is broken).
cited_not_measured.source: Angular Signal Forms guide + AsyncValidatorOptions docs; stated in the post, not separately asserted in this harness.

cited_not_measured.claim: zoneless + Vitest became Angular defaults in v21, not v22.
cited_not_measured.source: Angular release notes; contextual, not a Signal-Forms behavior.

honest_limitations: Re-run counts are measured as signal/subscription re-executions in a headless zoneless TestBed (jsdom), NOT as real component DOM change-detection cycles. The post argues granularity, never absolute milliseconds.
Signal Forms is newly stable in v22; this harness exercises the core state/validation contracts, not full feature parity with Reactive Forms.
programmatic value.set() does not auto-mark dirty; experiment C triggers touched explicitly via markAsTouched().
